title: Spin-torque microwave detectors of positive rectangular pulse signals
authors: V. Prokopenko, O. Shtanko, I. Sotnyk, O. Prokopenko
abstract: We analyze the performance of a spin-torque microwave detector (STMD) driven by positive rectangular current pulses $I(t)$ of various amplitudes $I_0$, durations $τ$, and repetition periods $T$ and reveal two distinct regimes of STMD operation. In the first (linear) regime, the time-averaged voltage across the detector, $U_{\rm dc}$, changes linearly with the pulse amplitude $I_0$ and depends on the ratio $τ/T$: $U_{\rm dc} \sim I_0 (τ/T)$. This regime is observed for a wide range of pulse amplitudes $I_0$ in the case of in-plane (IP) magnetization dynamics and for rather small pulse amplitudes $I_0 \le I_{\rm th}$ in an STMD with out-of-plane (OOP) magnetization dynamics. The other (nonlinear) regime is characterized by voltage jumps and drops and is observed only in a structure with OOP magnetization dynamics for input pulses with short repetition periods and large amplitudes $I_0 \ge I_{\rm th}$. We believe that the linear regime of STMD operation can be used to unambiguously detect input pulse parameters, which could be important for the development and optimization of spintronic devices capable of detecting and processing non-harmonic (e.g., digital) microwave signals.
summary: This work investigates how a spin-torque microwave detector (STMD) responds to rectangular current pulses, revealing two operational regimes. The linear regime allows for the unambiguous detection of input pulse parameters via a predictable linear relationship between the measured DC voltage and the pulse parameters. This suggests practical utility for developing spintronic devices capable of digital signal processing.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the performance of a spin-torque microwave detector (STMD) when driven by positive rectangular current pulses to detect and process non-harmonic (digital) microwave signals.
main_result: The STMD exhibits two regimes: a linear regime where the DC voltage is proportional to $I_0 (	au/T)$, which is ideal for parameter detection, and a nonlinear regime characterized by voltage jumps/drops in the out-of-plane magnetization case.
method: The analysis involves deriving the time-averaged voltage $U_{dc}$ from the time-dependent voltage $U(t) = I(t)R(t)$ by solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equation for magnetization dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is an STMD based on Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (MTJs). Magnetization dynamics are modeled using the macrospin approximation governed by the LLG equation, considering both in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OOP) magnetization dynamics.
key_observables: Time-averaged DC voltage ($U_{dc}$), instantaneous voltage ($U(t)$), and the dependence of $U_{dc}$ on input pulse amplitude ($I_0$), duration ($	au$), and repetition period ($T$).
important_parameters: The linear regime is characterized by $U_{dc} \sim I_0 (	au/T)$; the nonlinear regime is associated with a threshold amplitude $I_{th}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the macrospin approximation for magnetization dynamics and assumes fixed polarization magnetization along $\hat{x}$.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the time dependence of voltage and magnetization for IP and OOP regimes. Figure 3 plots $U_{dc}$ versus $I_0$ for various $	au$ and $T$, showing linear behavior in the IP case and nonlinear jumps in the OOP case.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the STMD response to periodic rectangular pulses, deriving the governing equations, identifying two distinct operational regimes (linear/IP and nonlinear/OOP), and concluding that the linear regime offers unambiguous parameter detection.
why_interesting: While the core physics is spintronics, the analysis of non-linear dynamics and the identification of a linear operating regime for signal processing parallels concepts in open quantum systems where linear response theory is used to characterize system response to weak perturbations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Layout of a circular STMD consisting of free and pinned magnetic layers separated by a dielectric spacer. When an input pulse current I(t) is applied to the structure, it excites the magnetization dynamics, M(t), described by the normalized magnetization vector m ≡m(t) = M(t)/|M(t)|. The vector m precesses along a particu- lar trajectory, depending on the configuration of the bias dc magnetic field Bdc: an in-plane trajectory (red dotted curve) for an in-plane field Bdc = BIP dc (red dashed arrow) and an out-of-plane trajectory (blue dotted curve) for an out-of-plane field Bdc = BOOP dc (blue dashed arrow). (b) A set of plots illustrating the principle of the device oper- ation...

FIG. 2. Typical time dependence of (a) the input rectangular pulse current I(t), (c) the x-component of dynamic magnetization, mx(t), (d) the device magnetoresistance R(t), and (b, e) the voltage U(t) generated across the device. Solid red lines and dashed blue lines in (b)-(e) correspond to the IP and OOP regimes of STMD operation, respectively. Picture (f) shows the trajectory of magnetization motion (red line for an in-plane regime and blue line for an out-of-plane regime) on a surface of unit sphere |m| = 1. Calculations performed for pulse parameters I0 = 0.5 mA, τ = 2 ns, T = 4 ns. All other calculation parameters are indicated in the text.

FIG. 3. The detector output dc voltage Udc as a function of the amplitude I0 of input pulse current calculated numerically for different pulse durations τ and a pulse repetition period of T = 2 ns (a, c) and T = 4 ns (b, d). All calculations were performed for an STMD with typical parameters (see the main text for details), with IP magnetization dynamics (a, b) and OOP magnetization dynamics (c, d). The curves shown in (a, b, d) demonstrate good agreement with the approximate linear dependence Udc ∼I0(τ/T), however, the curves in (c) contain voltage jumps and drops, which are typical for the nonlinear regime of device operation.
